name: Add a Label Alias to repo-standards
summary: How to add a new label mapping to label-aliases.yml in convergent-systems-co/repo-standards so the label-cleanup workflow can migrate it across all org repos.

how_to_profile.task: Add a new label alias mapping to the org-wide label cleanup workflow

body.inline:
## When to do this

Do this when you have renamed a label (or want to retire an old label in favor of a new one) and need the change to propagate automatically to all repositories in the `convergent-systems-co` org.

## Steps

### 1. Locate label-aliases.yml

```bash
gh api repos/convergent-systems-co/repo-standards/contents/label-aliases.yml \
  --jq '.download_url' | xargs curl -s
```

Or clone repo-standards and open `label-aliases.yml` directly.

### 2. Add your mapping

The file format is a list of `{from, to}` pairs:

```yaml
aliases:
  - from: "old-label-name"
    to: "new-label-name"
  - from: "bug"
    to: "type/bug"
```

Add your new mapping at the end of the list. The `from` value is the label to be replaced; `to` is the label it should become.

### 3. Ensure the target label exists in the label definition file

Check that `to` is listed in `labels.yml` (or equivalent) in repo-standards. If not, add it there too. The cleanup workflow applies aliases only to labels that exist in the canonical definition.

### 4. Commit and open a PR

```bash
git add label-aliases.yml
git commit -m "chore: add alias <old> -> <new>"
git push origin feat/label-alias-<new>
gh pr create --repo convergent-systems-co/repo-standards
```

### 5. Merge and observe propagation

After the PR merges, the label-cleanup workflow runs on a schedule (or you can trigger it manually via `gh workflow run`). Confirm propagation on a sample repo:

```bash
gh label list --repo convergent-systems-co/<sample-repo> | grep <new-label-name>
```

## Notes

- Label aliases are additive. Removing a mapping from the file does not undo a completed migration.
- If a repo has open issues or PRs with the old label, GitHub will update them automatically when the label is renamed via the API.
